# MPEG-TS interoperability fixtures

## Why this directory exists

All other tests in this package validate the code against itself: unit tests
check each structure against hand-computed bytes from ISO/IEC 13818-1, and the
round-trip tests prove that the Writer and the Reader agree with each other.
None of that catches a shared misreading of the specification: if both halves
made the same mistake, every self-test would pass while real transport streams
failed to parse.

The files in this directory close that gap. They are generated by FFmpeg — the
muxer that produces the vast majority of transport streams in the wild — and
`fixture_test.go` requires our Reader to parse them correctly. Passing these
tests means the package is interoperable with the outside world, not merely
self-consistent.

## What each fixture tests

| File | Contents | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| `h264.ts` | 1 s of H.264, 25 frames, keyframe first, no B-frames | Track discovery via PAT/PMT (stream type 0x1B), access unit reassembly across TS packets, keyframe and random-access detection on real muxer output |
| `h265.ts` | 1 s of H.265, 25 frames, IRAP first | The same demux path for HEVC (stream type 0x24), including IRAP keyframe detection |
| `h264_bframes.ts` | H.264 encoded with B-frames | PTS/DTS handling under reordering: DTS must stay monotonic while PTS jumps backwards — the only test exercising distinct PTS and DTS values from a real encoder |

## Regenerating the fixtures

Run from this directory. Encoders may produce slightly different output across
FFmpeg versions; if frame counts change, update the assertions in
`fixture_test.go` accordingly.

```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=duration=1:size=320x240:rate=25 \
  -c:v libx264 -profile:v baseline -g 25 -f mpegts h264.ts

ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=duration=1:size=320x240:rate=25 \
  -c:v libx265 -x265-params keyint=25 -f mpegts h265.ts

ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=duration=1:size=320x240:rate=25 \
  -c:v libx264 -bf 2 -f mpegts h264_bframes.ts
```

## Manual Writer validation checklist

The fixtures validate the Reader against FFmpeg; the Writer is validated in CI
only by round-tripping through our own Reader. Before tagging a release,
validate Writer output against external tools as well:

1. Produce a file by remuxing a fixture through this package
   (Reader -> Writer), or by writing frames from an encoder.
2. `ffprobe -show_frames out.ts` reports clean frames, correct
   `pict_type`/`key_frame`, and monotonic timestamps with no errors.
3. `ffplay out.ts` and VLC play the file from the start.
4. Optional: TSDuck `tsanalyze out.ts` reports no continuity or PCR errors.
